text.p: - Moscow tax collecting offices will work longer hours in March with assistants to help fill in tax forms, says a front page report. April 1 is the deadline for Russians to submit income declarations.

- Chubais has been "honoured" with the name of "fire-raiser" and deputies are afraid he will "burn" the Duma, says the paper in a reference to a parliamentary resolution on Wednesday criticising the government reshuffle.

-Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko came out with an idea on Wednesday to develop closer cooperation between Russia and Belarus with China to oppose NATO expansion in eastern Europe, says the paper.
- Chubais's restoration to government has boosted interest for rouble in Russia's financial markets, a banking official is quoted as saying.

- While the United States welcome the appointment of Chubais to the government, Russia's State Duma is protesting as his name symbolises collapse, comments the paper on the reshuffle in the government. A front page cartoon shows President Boris Yeltsin signing a decree while a snake with Chubais's head winds round the president and whispers in his ear.
- If the government does not undertake a decisive attack on reactionary forces the example of Albania will infect Russia.
- About 90 percent of video films sold in Russia are pirate copies.
